In [[mathematics]], the '''Brauer–Nesbitt theorem''' can refer to  several different theorems proved by [[Richard Brauer]] and [[Cecil J. Nesbitt]] in the [[representation theory]] of [[finite group]]s.

In [[modular representation theory]],
the '''Brauer–Nesbitt theorem on blocks of defect zero''' states that a character whose order is divisible by the highest power of a prime ''p'' dividing the order of a finite group remains irreducible when reduced mod ''p'' and vanishes on all elements whose order is divisible by ''p''. Moreover, it belongs to a [[block (representation theory)|block]] of [[defect zero]]. A block of defect zero contains only one [[ordinary character]] and only one [[modular character]].

Another version states that if ''k'' is a field of characteristic zero, ''A'' is a ''k''-algebra, ''V'', ''W'' are semisimple ''A''-modules which are finite dimensional over ''k'', and Tr<sub>''V''</sub> = Tr<sub>''W''</sub> as elements of Hom<sub>k</sub>(''A'',k), then ''V'' and ''W'' are isomorphic as ''A''-modules.

Let <math>G</math> be a group and <math>E</math> be some field. If <math>\rho_i:G\to GL_n(E),i=1,2</math>  are two finite-dimensional semisimple representations such that the characteristic polynomials of <math>\rho_1(g)</math> and <math>\rho_2(g)</math> coincide for all <math>g\in G</math>, then <math>\rho_1</math> and <math>\rho_2</math> are isomorphic representations. If <math>char(E)=0</math> or <math>char(E)>n</math>, then the condition on the characteristic polynomials can be changed to the condition that Tr<math>\rho_1(g)</math>=Tr<math>\rho_2(g)</math> for all <math>g\in G</math>. 

As a consequence, let <math>\rho:Gal(K^{\rm{sep}}/K)\to GL_n(\overline{\mathbb{Q}}_l)</math> be a semisimple (continuous) <math>l</math>-adic representations of the absolute Galois group of some field <math>K</math>, unramified outside some finite set of primes <math>S\subset M_K</math>. Then the representation is uniquely determined by the values of the traces of <math>\rho(Frob_p)</math> for <math>p\in M_K^0-S</math> (also using the Chebotarev density theorem). 

==References==
*Curtis, Reiner, ''Representation theory of finite groups and associative algebras'', Wiley 1962. 
*Brauer, R.; Nesbitt, C. ''On the modular characters of groups.'' Ann. of Math. (2) 42, (1941). 556-590.
